verify.note: One machine through four advances and a restart against the original ROM reading the Ocean tape signal. Replay each recording using the graphics code and colour pages installed by the single NEX.

status.title: The Simpsons: Bart vs. the Space Mutants (five-level test copy)
status.build: v1.1 test copy. One NEX for the Ocean 128K tape. Default sprites and painted Enhanced.
status.software: Scripted advances through all five levels and restart against the original tape loader. The recordings cover each level separately.
status.next: Unaided end-to-end play and a physical Next test.

techniques.target: the game's draw routine and both screens unchanged; each figure's sprites lie on its own pixels, switched in one attribute run at the game's flip
a shape's bytes give its keys (sum, 16-bit hash, size); the index page maps them to the picture's strips, sent whole to the pattern port
two pattern sets of 64; the listed attributes in one run at the flip, the last list's sprites beyond them off
the draw pass gets the original's R and gives it back; an inline form at the shape and the width loop, where the stack pointer is the data pointer
28 MHz for the draw pass, the game's speed back before its return
one window a draw pass; each draw adds its time by width, rows, pre-shift kind and clip (fitted per level)
alt ROM image 0 = the 128K ROM 0 whose bytes the game reads as data; the hooks from 0x2000 in both images

pacing.coverage: Five whole recordings, one a level (102,687 frames); each draw's time fitted from them by width code, rows, pre-shift kind and clip; hook time on the simulator's line clock. No JNext or hardware timing.
pacing.result: The draw pass runs at 28 MHz and its own time is waited out in one window. The hooks take 0.12% to 0.24% of a recording's time less than the passes they stand for; 2% to 4% of passes land more than 3 video lines from the original's time.

dependencies.coverage: The draw routine, its eight width loops, the flip and the erase read in level 1 and found by their bytes in the other four loads; the interrupt handler (the whole game runs in it) over every recording; the ROM bytes read as data.
dependencies.result: Nothing of the game's memory or screens changes, so nothing that reads them can differ. The handler reads R (music), so every hook leaves R as the original. The game reads 128K ROM 0 bytes as data: that ROM is alt image 0.

feasibility.decision: Keep the game loader and serve all six CODE blocks per level from RAM. Boot the first recording. Keep the five published patches.
feasibility.next_experiment: Play through the four level endings on a physical Next.
